update.headline: Tech led a risk-on day even as headline inflation re-accelerated; the broader tape still shows one-month duration pressure, a stronger-dollar impulse, and narrow equity leadership.
update.economy: Inflation was sticky on the headline measures: CPI y/y rose to 3.71% from 3.54%, a 0.17 pp increase, and CPI m/m rose to 0.4% from 0.07%, a 0.33 pp increase. PCE y/y rose to 3.42% from 3.36%, a 0.06 pp increase, and PCE m/m rose to 0.31% from 0.05%, a 0.26 pp increase. Core inflation was mixed: Core CPI y/y edged down to 2.76% from 2.79%, a -0.03 pp change, but Core CPI m/m rose to 0.29% from 0.22%, a 0.07 pp increase; Core PCE y/y rose to 3.01% from 2.98%, a 0.03 pp increase, and Core PCE m/m rose to 0.25% from 0.13%, a 0.12 pp increase. Labor softened at the margin, with unemployment up to 4.2% from 4.1%, a 0.1 pp increase, and payrolls y/y down to 0.31% from 0.34%, a -0.03 pp change. Industrial production y/y improved to 1.42% from 1.13%, a 0.29 pp increase. Consensus and surprise are unavailable in the snapshot. snapshot.data_gaps: none. snapshot.model_note: none.
update.asset_classes: Equities rallied on the day, led by long-duration growth: QQQ gained 1.02% and XLK gained 1.01%, ahead of SPY at 0.74%. That fits the theme of narrow technology leadership: over 1 month, XLK is up 8.96% and QQQ is up 5.8%, while XLF is down -6.9%, XLY is down -3.99%, XLV is down -3.55%, and XLI is down -1.37%. Rates were mixed across horizons: DGS2 fell -10.0 bp on the day and DGS10 fell -5.0 bp, which helped growth equities, but the one-month move remains a duration headwind with DGS2 up 39.0 bp and DGS10 up 45.0 bp; TLT is down -5.07% over 1 month, IEF is down -3.06%, and LQD is down -2.92%. Credit is not confirming broad risk strength, with HYG down -2.35% over 1 month. Commodities were weak in precious metals as higher one-month yields and dollar strength continued to bite: GLD fell -0.68% on the day and is down -5.62% over 1 month, while GC_F is down -5.72% over 1 month. Oil softened on the day, with USO down -1.77% and CL_F down -1.9%, though USO remains up 4.41% over 1 month and CL_F is up 0.11%. FX still shows a stronger-dollar backdrop over 1 month: EURUSD is down -2.83%, GBPUSD is down -1.8%, AUDUSD is down -3.39%, and USDCAD is up 3.32%; USDJPY is up 1.39% over 1 month.
update.predictions_changed: No regime prediction changed. The growth model was unchanged, with old and new both 91.16%, and the gate marked unchanged. The inflation model was also unchanged, with old and new both 25.58%, and the gate marked unchanged. Because the gates did not change, the snapshot should be read as no update to the regime calls, not as a new refit-driven forecast.

themes_touched.title: Narrow technology leadership versus cyclical weakness
themes_touched.text: Still active. The day was risk-on, but leadership remained concentrated: QQQ rose 1.02% and XLK rose 1.01%, while SPY rose 0.74%. Over 1 month the divergence is larger, with XLK up 8.96% versus XLF down -6.9%, XLY down -3.99%, XLV down -3.55%, and XLI down -1.37%. This keeps the equity tape dependent on technology rather than broad cyclical participation.

themes_touched.title: Duration pressure and stronger-dollar stress
themes_touched.text: Still active, though there was a short-term rates reprieve. DGS2 fell -10.0 bp on the day and DGS10 fell -5.0 bp, supporting growth equities, but over 1 month DGS2 is up 39.0 bp and DGS10 is up 45.0 bp. The pressure is visible in TLT down -5.07%, IEF down -3.06%, LQD down -2.92%, and GLD down -5.62% over 1 month. FX also supports the stronger-dollar theme, with EURUSD down -2.83%, GBPUSD down -1.8%, AUDUSD down -3.39%, and USDCAD up 3.32% over 1 month.

sector_reads.text: Energy is still a short-term pullback inside a strong long-term uptrend, not a reversal. XLE is up 1.26% over 1 week but down -2.93% over 1 month, with -3.77 pp relative 1-month performance. The longer trend remains strong: XLE is up 18.94% over 3 months, 7.42% over 6 months, and 44.64% over 12 months, with 28.26 pp relative 12-month performance. Oil’s day weakness, with USO down -1.77% and CL_F down -1.9%, explains the near-term drag, but USO is still up 4.41% over 1 month.

Financials remain the weakest cyclical pocket and the move looks like renewed downside within a range, not a pullback inside leadership. XLF is down -2.46% over 1 week, -6.9% over 1 month, and -4.38% over 3 months, with -7.74 pp relative 1-month performance. The 12-month gain is only 1.77% and relative 12-month performance is -14.61 pp, consistent with the long-label of range-bound rather than an established uptrend.

Industrials are in a short-term pullback inside a fading longer uptrend. XLI is down -0.28% over 1 week, -1.37% over 1 month, and -8.17% over 3 months, with -2.21 pp relative 1-month performance. The sector is still up 4.31% over 6 months and 11.76% over 12 months, but relative 12-month performance is -4.62 pp and the long label is uptrend, fading. This looks like a pullback with trend risk, not a confirmed reversal yet.

Health care’s short-term weakness has deepened, but it still reads as a pullback inside a longer uptrend. XLV is down -2.65% over 1 week and -3.55% over 1 month, with -4.39 pp relative 1-month performance. Longer-term returns remain positive at 3.0% over 3 months, 14.13% over 6 months, and 17.76% over 12 months, with 1.38 pp relative 12-month performance. The divergence argues for correction rather than reversal, though the near-term tone has worsened.

Technology remains the clear leadership sector. XLK is up 1.8% over 1 week, 8.96% over 1 month, 8.97% over 3 months, 47.28% over 6 months, and 41.12% over 12 months. Relative performance is also strong at 8.12 pp over 1 month and 24.74 pp over 12 months. The short label is up, fading, so momentum may be moderating, but this is not a reversal.

Consumer discretionary weakness is continuation of a downtrend, not a pullback. XLY is down -0.47% over 1 week, -3.99% over 1 month, and -6.55% over 3 months, with -4.83 pp relative 1-month performance. The long-term picture is also weak, with XLY down -7.98% over 12 months and -24.36 pp relative 12-month performance. The sector did rise 1.13% on the day, but that looks like a bounce within a downtrend rather than a reversal.
